newsitem.title: USA: Safeway's deadline for Vons approaches.
newsitem.headline: Safeway's deadline for Vons approaches.

text.p: Vons Cos Inc. is widely expected to soon agree to merge with Safeway Inc., creating the nation's second largest supermarket chain, analysts said Friday, although some still believe a higher bid is in the offing.

"I continue to think the most sensible outcome is an agreement between the two. The offer might be improved slighty, but it would surprise me if Vons rejected Safeway's bid and the deal got hostile," said one arbitrageur.
Safeway already owns a third of Vons' stock and the two firms share directors. Safeway on Oct. 30 offered to issue 1.34 shares for each Vons share it does not already own.
"We would appreciate hearing from you within two weeks regarding your willingess to negotiate terms of the proposal," Safeway said in the letter to the Vons board on Oct. 30.
Vons has declined to comment since its Oct. 30 statement that said a board of outside directors will study the offer.
"It's a fairly healthy offer and it will be difficult for anyone to top," said Ed Comeau, an analyst with Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
"Since it's fairly priced, one could conclude that it will happen," said Comeau.
The deal also has the backing of Kohlberg Kravis & Co., which owns 52 percent of Safeway. KKR has a history of entering into friendly supermarket deals.
In addition, KKR General Partner Robert MacDonnell is a director of both Safeway and Vons. KKR executive James Greene is a director of both.
Safeway Chairman Peter Magowan and President Steve Burd also sit on both boards.
Nevertheless, one arbitrageur said if Vons does not respond by Wednesday, the ball is in Safeway's court and it could turn into a hostile takeover battle.
Safeway's stock rose 12.5 cents to $42.375, while Vons gained 12.5 cents to $54.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
